To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
multicast and caching are complementary, and that the best overall performance can be achieved by using both.
hierarchical caching is more effective than multicast for documents that change slowly or not at all.

hierarchical caching gives lower bandwidth usage and lower latency than multicast, except when the document changes frequently or is updated randomly, and in these cases multicast gives better performance.

improving the performance of the Internet by reducing the bandwidth usage and latency in the delivery of Web documents.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best overall performance for WWW distribution is obtained by using a combination of multicast and hierarchical Web caching.
CMP is a good alternative for the distribution of frequently updated documents.
the Internet should implement both hierarchical caching and multicast, and use them together in a complementary manner.

the best performance is achieved when a document can be cached and can be multicast.
